title: Mini Crackme: length + sum check (2026-09-23)
blurb:
Target: Windows x86-64 (MSVC calling convention: RCX = pointer to a null-terminated ASCII string). Find an input string that makes check return 1.

check:
        xor     r8d, r8d        ; r8d = length counter
        xor     r9d, r9d        ; r9d = sum accumulator
.loop:
        movzx   eax, byte ptr [rcx + r8]
        test    eax, eax
        jz      .end
        add     r9d, eax
        inc     r8d
        jmp     .loop
.end:
        cmp     r8d, 5
        jne     .fail
        cmp     r9d, 500
        jne     .fail
        mov     eax, 1
        ret
.fail:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

What string(s) satisfy check?

--- Answer ---

"ddddd" (five copies of the character 'd') passes.

Explanation: The loop walks the string until the null terminator, counting bytes into r8d and summing their ASCII values into r9d, so check requires exactly two things: length == 5 and byte-sum == 500. 'd' is ASCII 0x64 = 100 decimal, so five 'd' characters give length 5 and sum 5*100=500, satisfying both comparisons. Any other 5-character string whose bytes sum to 500 also works, since the check only constrains the total, not individual characters.
